Subject: Post-demo: SentraHealth dedicated pilot — initial recap

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo window today. Quick run-down of what we captured and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist: 

- Goal: validate dedicated capacity for your real-time clinical-summaries product (low-latency streaming + high aggregate throughput during business hours).
- SLO targets you mentioned: p95 generation latency <= 75ms on 256-token streaming summaries; end-to-end streaming tail <= 120ms.
- Target throughput: sustained ~80 QPS, with short bursts to 200 QPS during morning batch periods.
- Concurrency: expect ~250 concurrent connections (streaming sessions), typical payloads 64–256 tokens.

Open items we suggested collecting for a sizing pass: 
1) Representative prompt set (we only need 50–100 samples across short/long summaries).
2) Live traffic pattern (hourly QPS for a typical weekday).
3) Any infra constraints: VPC-only, approved GPU types, or strict KMS/HSM requirements.

Next steps (action owners):
- Alex: share prompt samples + hourly QPS by Thu 3/10.
- Priya: confirm procurement lead + timeline for a 6-week pilot.
- Diego: assemble dedicated pilot sizing contrasts (A100 vs H100 vs 80GB L3) and a lightweight runbook for bench runs.
- Marissa / Ben: stand by for ops handoff for pilot orchestration.

I'll attach a preliminary sizing matrix and the perf-run commands we typically run — these are just for the pilot lab. If anything above reads wrong, correct here and we'll adjust.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez

- Concurrency: 300 sessions is a safer upper bound. Many sessions are long-lived (60–120s) while streaming.

Alex — great, thanks for the prompt samples and the traffic profile. I updated the sizing matrix (attached) and added a reserved-throughput framing per GPU class; summary below: 

Summary (very condensed):
- A100 40GB (dense FP16 / int8 paths): best cost/per-token for sustained batchy loads; one pod (8x A100 shared) can cover ~2200 tokens/s @ 256-token med summaries (est.). Reserved QPS mapping: ~110 QPS sustained per 8-GPU pod at p95 ~90ms when batching is enabled.
- H100 80GB (windowed-attention, faster kernel set): lower tail latency for streaming, better headroom for concurrency; one H100 instance (4x H100 pool) gives ~150 QPS sustained with p95 ~60–75ms for streaming summaries at 256 tokens.
- 80GB L3 (cost-optimized 80GB class / quantized): good for cost-constrained pilots with predictable patterns; expect slightly higher p95 (100–140ms) but lower spend.

Key tradeoffs:
- Tail latency: H100 pools win for p95 streaming targets without aggressive batching.
- Cost: A100 pods excel once you can leverage continuous batching + KV cache reuse.
- Concurrency: if you need 300 persistent streams, favor H100 pools or mix H100 headroom with A100 for background throughput.

Attachments included: sentra_pilot_sizing_matrix.xlsx (detailed per-GPU reserved-throughput rows), pilot_perf_run_commands.txt (bench commands and flags), rt-streaming-latency-samples.json (sample traces).

Proposed next pilot milestones: 
1) Week 0: exchange access + small dataset (you've done this).
2) Week 1: Redwood runs baseline bench (we'll run the attached commands against a 2-hour window).
3) Week 2: pair-run with SentraHealth on live-ish traffic (shadow traffic from your staging).
4) Week 3–4: scale to sustained 80 QPS pilot with SLO telemetry collection; adjust reserved units.

Alex — will schedule the bench window. Marissa / Ben — want to flag any ops prerequisites (VPC peering, egress rules) we should surface to Sentra?

Diego
Senior AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sentra_pilot_sizing_matrix.xlsx, pilot_perf_run_commands.txt, rt-streaming-latency-samples.json

Alex / team — I dug into the numbers in the sentra_pilot_sizing_matrix.xlsx and added a short note:

- Using your target of 256-token median summaries and 80 QPS sustained:
  - If you aim for A100 pods (8x40GB) with batching, plan initial reserved throughput at ~900k tokens/min (~15k tokens/s) which maps to ~110 QPS sustained at p95 ~90ms per 8-GPU pod (matches Diego's note). Two pods gives a comfortable headroom for background jobs.
  - For H100 pools (4x80GB), one pool maps to ~150 QPS sustained at p95 ~65ms; recommend starting with 1 H100 pool + 1 A100 pod for cost/latency balance.

Cost framing (very rough):
- 1 H100 pool + 1 A100 pod — expected pilot monthly run-rate ~ 3.5–4x higher than A100-only but gives p95 headroom and reduces SLO risk.
- A100-only with aggressive batching reduces monthly spend but may require more orchestration to maintain tail during bursts.

Recommendation: run the bench on Tue 14 Mar as Marissa suggested; capture p50/p95/p99 for token latencies and token/sec across concurrency sweep (50 -> 300). We'll use those traces to finalize reserved-units mapping and commit recommendation.

I'll be on the bench run and will instrument the KV-cache warmup scenarios.

Karthik Iyer
